newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record high of 13,217.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng leaps to record high of 13,217.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumped 160 points to a record high of 13,217 in early trade on Wednesday, prompted by Wall Street's latest record smashing performance and bullish local sentiment, brokers said.
"The Dow's 50-point gain added some strength to the Hong Kong market," said Teresa Wong, chief dealer at DBS Securities. "But the market needs to shake off these placement rumours."
Turnover jumped to more than HK$1.00 billion in the first 15 minutes of trade.

On Tuesday, the Hang Seng Index soared to a new intraday high of 13,183.01, then slid 130 points to close at 13,056.93 after rumours of share placements by the index's largest blue chips flew through the market in the afternoon.
Brokers said the surge at the open may have been due in part to short covering by those who sold after Tuesday's placement rumours as well as the bullish performance of the Dow.
The political and economic picture in Hong Kong and overseas is also favourable to the local market, they added.

"We now have a very pro-business (political) environment, good fundamental picture, and the added benefit of poor performances in other Southeast Asian markets," said one Hong Kong based North American broker. "Where are the clouds going to come from? The Dow."

On Tuesday, the Dow Jones Industrial average set its 40th record closing high of the year and its ninth record out of the past 10 trading sessions and U.S. brokers are uncertain about the length and strength of this phase of the bull run.
Trading in Hang Seng Index futures was also brisk. The November contract traded between 13,140 and 13,220 in the first half hour of trading, but never at a premium to the market's highs.
All sectors rose. Properties led the way, followed by the commercial and industrial sector. H shares also soared with the market.
Sun Hung Kai Properties regained HK$1.50 to HK$93.75 and Swire Pacific put on HK$1.00 to HK$71.00.
Guangshen Railway led the H shares with a gain of HK$0.10 to HK$3.00.
